title: Pressure & Fluids at Rest
intro: From the sharp panga to the village water tower: pressure in solids, liquids and air, with siphons and hydraulics built by hand.

lessons.title: What Is Pressure? Force Spread Over Area
lessons.focus: P = F/A; sharp nail pierces, blunt one doesn't; sitting on one stone vs a flat board; units N/m² (pascal).
lessons.advanced: Compute the pressure under a 50 N nail tip of 0.1 mm²; compare with a 500 N student on two feet (300 cm²).

lessons.title: Pressure in Daily Life: Sharp, Wide, Deep
lessons.focus: Panga edge vs spine, high heels in mud, wide tractor tyres, heavy lorries vs murram roads; hooves comparison.
lessons.advanced: Explain why wide tyres 'float' a tractor on soft soil using numbers: double area, halve pressure.

lessons.title: Calculating Pressure: Feet, Hooves and Jerricans
lessons.focus: Measure your foot area on squared paper; compute standing pressures; full jerrican on its base.
lessons.advanced: One foot vs two vs tiptoe: compute all three pressures and relate to sinking in mud.

lessons.title: Pressure in Liquids I: The Jerrican with Three Holes
lessons.focus: Holes at three heights jet different distances; deeper = more pressure; pressure acts in all directions.
lessons.advanced: Measure jet ranges vs depth; explain the shape of the relationship qualitatively.

lessons.title: Pressure in Liquids II: P = ρgh and Dam Walls
lessons.focus: Build P=ρgh from a water column's weight; dam walls thicker at the base (Masinga, Thwake); units check.
lessons.advanced: Compute pressure at 10 m depth (ρ=1000, g=10); what force on a 1 m² sluice gate at that depth?

lessons.title: Water Finds Its Level: Communicating Vessels
lessons.focus: Connected tubes settle level regardless of shape; teapot spout physics; spirit-level alternative.
lessons.advanced: Explain with P=ρgh why the levels must match, including for two different-width arms.

lessons.title: Build: The Hose Water Level (Fundi's Tool)
lessons.focus: Clear tube + water makes a long-distance level; mark two posts at identical height across a slope; test against a spirit level.
lessons.advanced: Why must there be no air bubble in the tube? Quantify the error a 5 cm bubble could cause.

lessons.title: Build: The U-Tube Manometer
lessons.focus: Bend tubing into a U; water levels measure small pressures; measure lung pressure by gentle blowing; read mm of water.
lessons.advanced: Convert a 300 mm water difference into pascals using P=ρgh.

lessons.title: Air Has Weight: Atmospheric Pressure Exists
lessons.focus: Teacher demo: crush a tin with steam + cold water; rubber suckers stick; air presses ~100 kPa at sea level.
lessons.advanced: Atmospheric pressure ≈ 101 kPa: force on a 10 cm² tin lid? Why aren't we crushed?

lessons.title: Using Air Pressure: Straws, Syringes and Suckers
lessons.focus: Drinking through a straw is the atmosphere pushing; syringe filling; hook suckers; 'suction' is a myth — pressure difference is real.
lessons.advanced: Explain the maximum straw-lift height from P=ρgh with atmospheric pressure (≈10 m of water).

lessons.title: Altitude and Air Pressure: From the Coast to the Highlands
lessons.focus: Ears pop on the escarpment; sealed bottles swell when travelling down; boiling point drops in the highlands (cooking time!).
lessons.advanced: Nairobi ≈ 1660 m, ~84 kPa: why does ugali cooking take longer there? Link pressure to boiling point.

lessons.title: Build: A Bottle Barometer for Weather Watching
lessons.focus: Inverted bottle neck in water jar; falling water = rising pressure; keep a two-week weather log against observations.
lessons.advanced: Explain why temperature changes can fool a bottle barometer; propose a correction routine.

lessons.title: Pascal's Principle: Pressure Travels Through Fluids
lessons.focus: Squeeze a sealed bottle, water jets from all holes equally; pressure applied to enclosed fluid transmits undiminished.
lessons.advanced: State Pascal's principle and use it to derive the hydraulic force multiplication F2=F1·A2/A1.

lessons.title: Hydraulic Machines I: The Syringe Lift
lessons.focus: Two syringes + tube of water: small plunger lifts heavy load on big plunger; measure the multiplication.
lessons.advanced: Plungers 1 cm² and 10 cm²: ideal MA, and the distance trade when small plunger moves 10 cm.

lessons.title: Hydraulic Machines II: Brakes, Presses and Excavators
lessons.focus: Car brake circuits, jua kali press, excavator arms; why fluid not air (incompressibility); bleeding brakes story.
lessons.advanced: Explain why an air bubble in a brake line makes the pedal 'spongy' and dangerous.

lessons.title: Build: The Hydraulic Lift Challenge I
lessons.focus: Team build: syringe-and-tube lift raising a stone platform; document design choices.
lessons.advanced: Predict the maximum load from plunger areas and your measured push force.

lessons.title: Build: The Hydraulic Lift Challenge II — Test and Measure
lessons.focus: Competition: heaviest load lifted 2 cm; compute MA and efficiency; leak post-mortems.
lessons.advanced: Your lift achieved MA 6 vs ideal 10: name two loss mechanisms and one fix each.

lessons.title: Pressure in Gases: Particles on the Attack
lessons.focus: Pump a ball/tyre and feel it firm up; particles bombarding walls; pressure rises when volume shrinks (qualitative).
lessons.advanced: Use particle collisions to explain why a sealed balloon shrinks in cold water.

lessons.title: Squeezing Air: A Qualitative Boyle's Law
lessons.focus: Seal a syringe and push: volume halves, push-back roughly doubles; graphs for the older students.
lessons.advanced: Take volume vs pressure readings with stacked weights; test P·V ≈ constant from your data.

lessons.title: Levers vs Hydraulics: Choosing a Force Multiplier
lessons.focus: Compare builds from Units 6 and 7: which multiplier for which job (precision, distance, dirt, maintenance).
lessons.advanced: Write a selection guide: lifting 1 tonne 0.5 m in a muddy garage — lever, tackle or hydraulic? Justify.

lessons.title: Why Water Tanks Stand Tall: Gravity Supply
lessons.focus: Head of water creates pressure; village gravity schemes from hill springs; compute the pressure of a 10 m standpipe.
lessons.advanced: Tap is 15 m below tank surface: pressure in kPa and the jet speed estimate (Torricelli v=√2gh) at the tap.

lessons.title: Siphon Theory: The River That Climbs a Hill
lessons.focus: How a siphon starts and runs; the rising leg works because atmosphere pushes; the falling leg pulls; height limits.
lessons.advanced: Explain with pressures at the crest why the lift leg cannot exceed ~10 m for water.

lessons.title: Siphon Practice I: Starting Methods
lessons.focus: Fill-tube-first method, pump-start, and safe mouth-start with clean water only; empty a jerrican to a lower basin.
lessons.advanced: Why does the siphon stop when the upper end sucks air? Describe the pressure chain breaking.

lessons.title: Siphon Practice II: Cisterns, Furrows and Ponds
lessons.focus: Toilet cistern siphon anatomy; draining a flooded trench; siphon to move water over a bund into furrows.
lessons.advanced: Compare siphon vs pump for emptying a pit 1 m deep over a 2 m bund: which is cheaper and why?

lessons.title: Pressure Safety: Cookers, Cylinders and Sealed Tins
lessons.focus: Pressure cooker valve physics; never heat sealed containers; gas cylinder care; borehole cap dangers.
lessons.advanced: Cooker at 200 kPa absolute on a 6 cm diameter lid: compute the clamping force the valve system handles.

lessons.title: Measuring Big Pressures: Pumps and Tyre Gauges
lessons.focus: Bicycle pump anatomy (valve!); tyre gauge reads kPa/psi; pump up and measure; why small pumps make big pressures.
lessons.advanced: Pump barrel 3 cm bore, 200 N effort: compute the pressure it can generate in kPa and psi (1 psi ≈ 6.9 kPa).

lessons.title: Build: The Cartesian Diver
lessons.focus: Dropper in a capped bottle: squeeze and it dives; buoyancy + pressure + gas compressibility in one toy.
lessons.advanced: Explain the dive using air-pocket compression changing average density; predict behavior at constant squeeze.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Pressure Lab Stations
lessons.focus: Stations: jerrican jets, manometer, syringe lift, siphon, diver; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Capstone-style question: design a system to water a garden 20 m below a tank, with flow control; mark scheme included.
